subject: Co-engineering pact: PromptBridge SDK + Redwood tracing plug-in
messages:
From: Oliver Wang <oliver@promptbridge.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Co-engineering proposal: Redwood tracing plug for PromptBridge SDK

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I’m Oliver, Head of Integrations at PromptBridge. We’ve built a lightweight orchestration SDK used by ~120 ISVs to manage prompt routing, templating, and prompt-level telemetry. Several mutual customers have asked for better visibility into token-level cost and KV-cache behavior when they route model calls through Redwood.

We’d like to propose a co-engineering agreement: PromptBridge would integrate a Redwood tracing shim into our SDK (LangChain & LlamaIndex connectors) that emits standardized trace spans and cost-attribution metadata. Redwood would provide a short-lived engineering liaison, a test instance (staging API key), and documentation for runtime-compatible trace headers. In exchange, PromptBridge will co-brand the integration, include a recommended Redwood runtime binding, and commit to a joint launch blog + webinar.

High-level asks:
- Short-term: ship an SDK plugin and example notebooks (2–3 weeks of focused dev)
- Medium-term: maintain the plugin with minor patches; include Redwood in partner marketplace listing
- Commercial: modest referral credit or co-sell people-hours (open to structuring)

I’ve attached a draft scope matrix and proposed SOW to start the conversation. Could you loop in the right engineering contact and let us know if Redwood is open to a co-marketing launch?

Best,
Oliver
Head of Integrations, PromptBridge
attachments: PB-Redwood_scope_matrix.xlsx, PB-proposed_sow_v1.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Wang <oliver@promptbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-engineering proposal: Redwood tracing plug for PromptBridge SDK

Oliver — thanks for the clear outline and the attachments. I’ve looped in Marissa (integrations), Rishi (ISV partnerships), and Jordan (developer advocacy) to scope technical effort and the launch plan.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to run a quick feasibility pass against the LangChain & LlamaIndex hooks you reference (ETA EOD today).
2) We’ll provision a short-lived staging API key and a dedicated trace sampling configuration so we don’t hit production SLOs during the pilot.
3) Sync call this week to walk the SOW and clarify deliverables (30m).

Marissa — can you confirm whether a small shim that emits: span-type=prompt, token.count, model.variant, cache.hit=true/false plus a per-request cost_estimate is straightforward to add to your accepted tracer interface? Also flag any concerns about latency or serialization overhead.

Oliver — I’ll send calendar times for a 30m call. Happy to explore a referral credit model; Rishi can surface typical program terms.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Wang <oliver@promptbridge.io>; Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-engineering proposal: Redwood tracing plug for PromptBridge SDK

Thanks for the tag — did a quick read of the scope doc. High-level notes:

- The trace payload you describe maps well to our runtime telemetry (we already emit per-token counters and model variant metadata).
- Two compatibility questions we should confirm before committing dev time:
  1) LangChain/LlamaIndex hook placement: do you want a decorator-level integration (wrap LLM calls) or a lower-level transport hook? Decorator is quicker but misses some cross-call batching semantics.
  2) Sampling & sampling keys: if PromptBridge samples client prompts at 0.5% for production, we need a stable sampling key to ensure we observe cache behavior consistently across retries.

Suggested pilot scope (1.5–2 engineer-weeks):
- LangChain connector: decorator shim + example notebook + unit tests
- LlamaIndex: small adapter that forwards spans into Redwood tracer interface
- CI: e2e test that runs against our staging with a small corpus (we can share a saved prompt set)
- Docs: short integration guide + embed link to GH PR for tracing schema

Latency impact: should be sub-ms per request if we keep payloads minimal. I’ll prototype a tiny shim and open a draft PR against PromptBridge SDK repo if you can grant us contributor access or accept PRs.

—Marissa
Sr. Software Engineer, Integrations
attachments: none
From: Oliver Wang <oliver@promptbridge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-engineering proposal: Redwood tracing plug for PromptBridge SDK

Marissa — this is excellent; thank you. Answers inline:

1) Hook placement: decorator-level is fine for the first cut. We’ll accept that tradeoff to speed time-to-market. We do want a follow-up effort to capture batched calls (we can roadmap that).
2) Sampling: we can add a stable sampling key derived from customer_id+request_id hash at the SDK layer — we’ll surface that as a header so your tracing can correlate across retries.

We’ve shared contributor access to the GH repo (see PR 214 for the initial scaffolding). I’ve attached an updated scope matrix and the proposed SOW with a short co-marketing appendix.

If you can draft the PR, we’ll review and prioritize in the next sprint. For the commercial ask: PromptBridge is okay with a nominal referral credit (5% on first-year revenue from referrals) plus joint webinar marketing support. If Redwood prefers a different structure, we’re flexible.

Best,
Oliver
attachments: PB-Redwood_scope_matrix.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-engineering proposal: Redwood tracing plug for PromptBridge SDK — approval to proceed

Team — I like the scope and the low-friction commercial terms Oliver proposed. Approve moving forward with the pilot as outlined. Operational notes:

- Budget: authorize up to 2 engineer-weeks from Integrations (Marissa + 0.5E from Jordan for docs/examples).
- Staging: Soojin please create a staging API key with trace-sample config and set quota to protect production.
- Legal/Procure: Soojin — please loop Legal for a lightweight MOU that captures referral credit (PB-2027-045). We can sign a brief SOW after the pilot.
- Marketing: Jordan — prep a joint launch checklist and hold a draft blog ready; we’ll tentatively target late-April if pilot completes by mid-April.

Oliver — welcome aboard. Once Marissa opens the initial PR we’ll triage and provide reviewers.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, ISV Partnerships
